title: Microsoft Copilot: GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra rolling out
summary: Microsoft Copilot is expanding AI model options with GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra, rolling out across Cowork, Copilot Studio, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat. Astra requires enabling the OpenAI subprocessor. Users with appropriate licenses and configurations get default access; no action is needed but reviewing settings and guidance is recommended.
body:
What and Why

To give users more choice and flexibility when working with AI in Microsoft Copilot, we're expanding the set of AI models available in Microsoft Copilot.

GPT-6.2 Astra is rolling out with usage-based billing (UBB) in general availability to Cowork and Microsoft Copilot Studio and in Frontier to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat.

GPT-6.2 Sol is rolling out with usage-based billing in general availability to Cowork and Copilot Studio. It is also rolling out in general availability as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL) to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat. Limits apply to this model. They are designed to support broad day-to-day AI usage across organizations and are implemented in such a way that the vast majority of users are not expected to reach them. 

Rollout Schedule

General Availability:

- GPT-6.2 Astra: Rolling out to Cowork and Copilot Studio with UBB.- GPT-6.2 Sol: Rolling out to Cowork and Copilot Studio with UBB and to Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Chat as part of the USL. Frontier: 

- GPT-6.2 Astra: Rolling out to Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Chat.

Impact on Your Organization

Who is affected:

- Cowork and Copilot Studio (GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra): Users assigned a user subscription license (USL) with usage-based billing (UBB) enabled.- Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat (GPT-6.2 Sol): Users assigned a user subscription license (USL).- Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat in Frontier (GPT-6.2 Astra): Users assign a user subscription license who is enrolled in Frontier and has usage-based billing (UBB) enabled.- Access to GPT-6.2 Astra across all surfaces requires the OpenAI subprocessor to be enabled. Learn more: OpenAI as a subprocessor in Microsoft Online Services | Microsoft Learn. As a reminder, this setting only controls whether OpenAI models operated by OpenAI (provided by OpenAI as a subprocessor) can be used. OpenAI models operated by Microsoft (Azure OpenAI) aren't affected and remain available in Copilot regardless of this setting.

Platforms/Services:

- - Copilot Chat- Microsoft Word- Microsoft Excel- Microsoft PowerPoint- Copilot Cowork- Microsoft Copilot Studio

What will happen:

- Users will be able to select GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra using the model selector from supported Microsoft Copilot experiences.- The models are enabled by default for eligible licensed users who meet the applicable configuration requirements.

Action Required / Recommendations

No action is required for organizations that want users to access these models.

Recommended actions:

- Review whether the OpenAI subprocessor is enabled if you plan to make GPT-6.2 Astra broadly available to users. If disabled, this model will not be available.- Review your organization's AI usage guidance and communicate model availability to end users.- Inform helpdesk and support teams that users may encounter usage-limit notifications.- Update internal user documentation and training materials, as appropriate.

Compliance Considerations

Consideration Explanation Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra are additional AI models that users can select within Microsoft Copilot experiences to generate responses based on content and context available to the user through Copilot. Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Users gain access to new model choices, GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra, in supported Microsoft Copilot experiences. Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership? Access to GPT-6.2 Astra in Copilot depends on administrative configuration of the OpenAI subprocessor.
